facts.text: The upstream adaptor covers the Thorlabs MCM3000 and MCM3001 3-axis controllers
The controller's serial port is opened at 460800 baud with a 5 s read timeout
The supported stage table gives ZFM2020/ZFM2030 0.2116667 um/count within +/-12700 um and MMP-2XY 0.5 um/count within +/-25400 um
_legalize_move_um asserts that the requested position lies within the selected stage's position_limit_um
A position query is the 6-byte command 0A 04 <channel> 00 00 00; the 12-byte reply carries the channel at byte 6 and the signed 32-bit little-endian encoder count in its last four bytes
A move is the 12-byte command 53 04 06 00 00 00 <channel word> <signed 32-bit encoder count>
A relative move first refreshes the encoder position and then adds the requested offset before the limit check
The upstream class docstring says a stop function is not implemented
The vendor protocol defines an abrupt Stop Command with header 65 04, the channel byte and stop mode 0x01 that stops any type of motor move on the specified channel
The stage encoder is assumed to be zero at the centre of its range for the +/- position checks
Only the channels with a stage entry are available, and the constructor requires exactly three stage and reverse entries

operator_required.reason: the travel is a property of the stage the operator configures in the controller's stages argument: the clone tabulates ZFM2020/ZFM2030 at +/-12700 um and MMP-2XY at +/-25400 um (thorlabs_MCM3000.py:42-44) and _legalize_move_um refuses a target outside the selected entry (thorlabs_MCM3000.py:167-170), so the site declares the travel of each configured channel

safe_state.description: all configured channels stopped by the vendor's abrupt Stop Command (65 04, channel, stop mode 0x01)
